text: Continuous integration is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time someone makes a change, automated builds start immediately. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it by hand. As part of the process, the system also runs tests to make sure everything still works correctly. By doing this often, teams can catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines organise all these steps, from building to testing, in a clear and repeatable way. This helps developers save time, work together more smoothly, and release better software.
